margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Two frames on different metrics. (1) Three-year target for fiscal 2025 to 2027: restaurant-level profit (RLP) margin expansion of at least 50 bps a year (an RLP rate on Shack sales, with a horizon), plus adjusted EBITDA growth of low to high teens; stated by then CFO Fogertey, last reaffirmed 2026-02-26 by the VP FP&A, dropped from the Q2 2026 release and put 'under review' by the new CFO on 2026-08-05. (2) Live one-year guide (Q2 2026 shareholder letter): fiscal 2026 RLP margin 22.0% to 23.0%, adjusted EBITDA $225M to $235M on revenue $1.6B to $1.7B. The gap uses (2), an adjusted EBITDA margin, against VA EBITDA consensus (VA FY2025 EBITDA of $209.9M matches the company's adjusted EBITDA basis).

statements.quote: We're, you know, aiming to grow total revenue by a low teens %, expand our restaurant margins by 50 basis points a year, and grow our adjusted EBITDA anywhere between low teens-high teens %.

street.gap_assumption: December fiscal year, so VA labels equal company fiscal years. Gap compares the FY2026 guide midpoint ($230M adjusted EBITDA on $1.65B revenue = 13.94%) with VA FY2026 consensus (221.8M / 1,648.3M = 13.45%); consensus EBITDA sits below the low end of the $225M to $235M guide. The stale three-year RLP target (+50 bps a year through 2027) has no matching RLP consensus line in Baba and is under review, so it is not used for the gap. The street models only about 28 bps and 17 bps of EBITDA margin expansion in FY2027 and FY2028.
street.source: Baba data_financials summary consensus (Visible Alpha) cid 1000911; guide from 8-K EX-99.2 document_id 143992; margins and gap via data_compute

evidence_of_progress.note: Q1 2026: VA EBITDA 37.0M on 366.7M revenue (10.08%) vs Q1 2025 12.70%, -262 bps (includes $1.1M executive transition cost). Q2 2026: adjusted EBITDA margin 14.7%, -180 bps yoy, per 8-K EX-99.2 (document_id 143992); RLP margin 23.0% vs 23.9% in Q2 and 22.2% vs 22.4% for 26 weeks (same table). Beef inflation is the main stated driver. VA has not loaded Q2 2026. LTM 13.82% uses VA 2Q25 to 1Q26. The 2026 RLP guide of 22.0% to 23.0% means the 50 bps a year target is not being met in year two.

verdict: Cheap and broken (down 59%, 5th pctile) with a new external CFO, but the numeric margin frame is moving the wrong way: the 50 bps a year RLP target is under review after beef-driven margin declines, and the CEO is 28 months in.
open_questions: Does the 2027 planning update (date not given) cut or replace the 50 bps a year RLP target, and where does a new frame land versus the 13.73% FY2027 consensus EBITDA margin?
How much of the 2026 margin decline is beef (a commodity input) versus G&A and marketing investment (Project Catalyst, loyalty, 2% to 3% of revenue on marketing)?
Does Hook, a Portillo's and Domino's finance veteran, bring a G&A or unit-cost program with a number attached?
